say: Good morning, inquirers! Today you are code-breakers. A number went into a secret machine and something came out. Your job is to run the machine backwards and find the number that went in.
Remember our rule: notice it, test it, explain why.
I am a machine. Give me a number and I will tell you what comes out. Ready? You say 4, I say 12. You say 10, I say 30. What am I doing?
Now I only tell you what comes out: 18. What went in? How did you work it out?
Here are two machine cards: × 2 and + 6. If I put 4 in, what comes out? Now I swap the cards: + 6 first, then × 2. Will the same number come out? Thumbs up or down before we test it.
stuck: Stuck: write the machine as boxes and arrows, then put your partner’s OUT number in the last box.
Mixed up: “What was the LAST thing the machine did? Undo that first.”
Finished early: find an OUT number your partner can NOT undo with whole numbers. Why does it not work?

say: “Mystery number × 3, then + 4, gives 25. I go backwards. The last step was + 4, so I undo it first with − 4: 25 − 4 = 21. The step before was × 3, so I undo it with ÷ 3: 21 ÷ 3 = 7. Check forwards: 7 × 3 = 21, 21 + 4 = 25. ✓”

“Ben gave away 18 stamps, then bought 25, and now has 60. I draw the bars and start at the end. Before he bought 25 he had 60 − 25 = 35. Before he gave away 18 he had 35 + 18 = 53. Check: 53 − 18 = 35, 35 + 25 = 60. ✓”
“Mei gave away half her beads, then used 5. She has 9 left. The half she kept is 5 + 9 = 14. The other half is also 14. So she had 14 + 14 = 28.”

do: Ask: “What was the last step? What is its opposite?”
Ask: “Show me your check going forwards. Do you get the OUT number?”
Ask: “Point to your bar. Which part do you know? Which part is the mystery?”
stuck: Hint 1: “Draw the machine boxes. Write the OUT in the last box.”
Hint 2: “Cover the first step with your finger. Undo only the last step.”
Hint 3: “For bars: start from what is left now and put back each change, from the end to the start.”

do: Ask: “What was the last step? What is its opposite?”
Ask: “Show me your check going forwards. Do you get the OUT number?”
Ask: “Point to your bar. Which part do you know? Which part is the mystery?”
stuck: Hint 1: “Draw the machine boxes. Write the OUT in the last box.”
Hint 2: “Cover the first step with your finger. Undo only the last step.”
Hint 3: “For bars: start from what is left now and put back each change, from the end to the start.”

say: “To undo × 2, then + 6, with OUT 20, Mei takes away 6 first. Ali divides by 2 first. Who is right? Test both.”
ask: “To undo × 2, then + 6, with OUT 20, Mei takes away 6 first. Ali divides by 2 first. Who is right? Test both.”

Mei is right: 20 − 6 = 14, 14 ÷ 2 = 7, and 7 × 2 + 6 = 20. Ali gets 20 ÷ 2 = 10, 10 − 6 = 4, but 4 × 2 + 6 = 14, not 20. The last step happened last, so it must be undone first, like taking off shoes before socks.

say: “Today you ran machines backwards and drew before-and-after bars. Code-breakers always check forwards, and you did. Well done, inquirers!”

p2l5-title.note: Objective: Find a mystery number in two-step puzzles with +, −, × and ÷ by working backwards (undo the LAST step first with the opposite operation), check by going forwards, and use before-and-after bar models for stories where an amount changes. Materials: mini whiteboards, counters, paper cups, number machine cards (× 2, × 3, × 4, × 5, × 10, and + or − cards from 1 to 20), paper strips for bars. Online: machine cards are shown on the slides; children write on whiteboards and say the answer together on three; for bars they draw on paper or fold a paper strip into equal parts. Time plan: opening 0 to 1.5, sneak-peek puzzles 1.5 to 6, warm-up 6 to 10.5, explore 10.5 to 23.5, mini-lesson 23.5 to 35.5, brain break 35.5 to 38.5, worksheet teach slide 38.5 to 41, worksheet page 1 41 to 52.5, check together, page 1 52.5 to 55, short teaching 55 to 59.5, worksheet page 2 59.5 to 71, check together, page 2 71 to 73.5, flex (spare time) 73.5 to 76.5, talk time 76.5 to 81.5, exit ticket 81.5 to 86.5, looking back 86.5 to 88.5, closing and stamps 88.5 to 90. The Think harder and Go further slides are optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Kit ready at minute 0: ask families to put every item on the desk before the lesson starts (a 30-second check at the start). SPINE: Today's tool is Work backwards. Start at the end and undo each step. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

p2l5-tool.note: SPINE: Show for about 20 seconds, inside the opening. Today's tool is Work backwards. Start at the end and undo each step. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

p2l5-precheck.note: Minutes 1.5 to 6. Sneak-peek puzzles: two puzzles on the key idea of today, which the children have NOT learnt yet. Say out loud (about 28 words): "Two sneak-peek puzzles on ideas we have not learnt yet. Guessing is welcome, so is I do not know. Nobody is marked. Say your answer together on three." Question 1 is an access question: any child can try it with objects, a drawing or counting, so everyone has a first win (about 45 seconds). Question 2 is the thinking question (about 90 seconds). Then about 2 minutes for the answers slide and the move on. Answers are PRIVATE: each child writes on their own paper and says the answer together on three; nothing is held up to the camera. Do not raise whiteboards together, do not read answers out, do not name children. Q1 answer: 5 (5 + 7 = 12). Listen for: IN is what goes in and OUT is what comes out. Undo = do the opposite: 12 - 7. This is a first win for everyone. Q2 answer: 5 (5 doubled is 10, and 10 + 7 = 17). Listen for: Undo the last step first: 17 - 7 = 10, then half of 10 is 5. A guess that was tested (5 x 2 + 7 = 17) is just as good. At the end click to show the answers as "one way to think about it", without saying who had what. Ask only for volunteers: "Would anyone like to tell us how they started?" Invite the WHOLE group at once, never one child: "When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation." Never announce who is on which page. Pairs are not split unless both children agree. Children can move either way at any time. Everyone joins explore, the mini-lesson, the check-together slides and talk time.

p2l5-warm1.note: Minutes 6 to 8.5. You are the machine. Three rounds only (about 2.5 minutes): two rounds of IN to OUT guesses, then one OUT to IN round. Pick a secret one-step rule (start with × 3). Children call IN numbers; you say the OUT. After two or three, ask for a guess. Point at the picture: IN 4, OUT 12 could be + 8 OR × 3, so test another IN (5 gives 15 for × 3 but 13 for + 8). Good rules to use: × 3, + 15, × 10, ÷ 2 (only give even IN numbers), − 20, × 5. Round three is the flip: give only an OUT ("My machine is × 5. OUT is 35. What went IN?" 7). Listen for children who already "do the opposite". A game of about 2.5 minutes: stop it on the clock even if the game is not finished.

p2l5-warm2.note: Minutes 8.5 to 10.5. Read each one aloud, give thinking time, whiteboards face down until 3, 2, 1 (then say the answer together on three; never read a board out), then click for the answer. Ask "How did you find it?" each time. 1) 18 ÷ 2 = 9. 2) 40 + 25 = 65. Spare questions in the guide table: I divide by 5 and get 4 (20); the opposite of × 4 is ÷ 4; I multiply by 3, then add 4, and get 19 (5: 19 − 4 = 15, 15 ÷ 3 = 5; do not teach it yet, see who tries 19 ÷ 3 first, that is today’s big idea). Ask quick questions 1 and 3 only (about 2 minutes): children answer by thumbs, hands, not by naming a child. The other questions are spare.

p2l5-explore1.note: Minutes 10.5 to 19.5. Pairs build a two-step machine from the cards (one × card from × 2, × 3, × 4, × 5, × 10, and one + or − card). Partner A chooses a start number (keep it from 1 to 10) and says only the OUT. Partner B works backwards, then they check by going forwards. Partners swap roles every round, so each child both chooses the secret number and works backwards (never one child always being the solver). (Swapping the order of the two cards is dropped from the explore: the teachorder slide and worksheet Q5 ask exactly that.) Online: the tutor runs the machine on the slide and children work back on whiteboards; then pairs in breakout rooms make their own. Go further (a second what-if, so nobody waits) is the box at the foot of this slide; the question is also posted in the chat when the pairs go to their breakout rooms. It is for ANY child who finishes the explore task or wants more: say it to the whole group as a choice, never as a prize, and never name who tries it. Pairs stay together unless both children agree to split. Answer: No: 5 + 7 = 12, doubled is 24. The order of the steps matters. Take it at the debrief only if a pair offers it.

p2l5-explore2.note: Minutes 19.5 to 23.5. Let pairs keep working, then gather them. Answers: 1) Undo the LAST card first with its opposite, then undo the first card. 2) ÷ 3 undoes × 3; + 8 undoes − 8. (Does the order of the cards matter? That is the teachorder slide and worksheet Q5, not asked here.) Ask a pair whose machine could not be undone with a whole number (for example ÷ 3 first, then OUT 7 with + 2: 5 is not in the 3 table) to share: what went wrong? Keep it moving (about 4 minutes in all): ask "how do you know?" on question 2 only; about 15 seconds of talk on the other questions.

p2l5-teach1.note: Minutes 23.5 to 25.5. Teach. Show 4 groups of 5 counters: "× 4 made 20." Now share the 20 back into 4 groups: 5 in each. "÷ 4 undid × 4." Do the same with + 6 and − 6. Think-aloud for the machine: "Something times 4 is 20. To go backwards I do the opposite of × 4, which is ÷ 4. 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Check: 5 × 4 = 20." Click for the answer.

p2l5-we1.note: Minutes 25.5 to 29. Click to reveal each step; ask the group to predict it first. Analogy: "In the morning you put on socks, then shoes. At night you take off the shoes first." The last step done is the first step undone. Watch for children who do 25 ÷ 3 first: it does not even give a whole number, which is a clue they went the wrong way.

p2l5-try1.note: Minutes 29 to 30. Write it, say the answer together on three, then click. One item: 15 + 5 = 20, 20 ÷ 2 = 10. Ask for the rule in words: "undo the last step first". (Items b and c are dropped: worksheet Q1 has the same types.)

p2l5-we2.note: Minutes 30 to 33.5. Click 1: the "Now" bar (bottom): 60 is the stamps he had before buying, plus the 25 he bought. Click 2: before buying he had 60 − 25 = 35. Click 3: before giving 18 away he had 35 + 18 = 53. Click 4: check forwards. Say: "We read the story forwards but we solve it backwards, from the bottom bar up." The bars stop children from adding 18 and 25 to 60 without thinking.

p2l5-try2.note: Minutes 33.5 to 34.5. Whiteboards. a) 30 + 12 = 42. b) Before the $15: 35 − 15 = $20. She went from $40 to $20, so she spent $20. Two items only: the bus item is dropped.

p2l5-key.note: Minutes 34.5 to 35.5. Say the key idea together. Common mistakes to watch for during the worksheet: (1) Doing the same step again instead of the opposite (27 × 2 instead of 27 ÷ 2). (2) Undoing in the wrong order: the first step first. (3) Bar stories: stopping at one part (one bag, one half) instead of the whole, or forgetting to undo one of the changes.

p2l5-break.note: Minutes 35.5 to 38.5. Three minutes: two of movement, one for a drink of water. Online: children stay in view of the camera and move in place. Keep the OUT numbers small (under 15).

p2l5-teachrule.note: Minutes 38.5 to 41. Teach before worksheet page 1 (Think harder 1 asks for a rule like this). Think-aloud: "I guess the × part first. If it is × 2, then IN 1 makes 2, and I need + 5 to reach 7. Now I test it on the other pair: 4 × 2 = 8, 8 + 5 = 13. Yes!" Then show that × 3 and × 4 also give 7 for IN 1 but fail the test. Point out: with IN 1 every guess works, so the second pair is what tells them apart. Do not tell them the worksheet rule.

p2l5-ws1.note: Minutes 41 to 52.5. Walk around. Ask "What was the last step? What is its opposite?" before giving any help. Q1(d) (× 4, then − 15) is marked ★ take-home on the page: children do it at home. For Q2a the last two columns need going backwards. For Q2b suggest a table of guesses like the one on the last slide. Say once, to everyone: "After question 3 you may choose: carry on, or try Think harder." Never say who is on which page. Invite the WHOLE group at once, never one child: "When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation." Pairs are not split unless both children agree.

p2l5-ws1ans.note: Minutes 52.5 to 55. Click after a pair explains (answer lines only). Q1(d) is a take-home star: the answer stays here for children to mark at home. Q1: a) 27 − 7 = 20, 20 ÷ 2 = 10. b) 40 ÷ 5 = 8, 8 + 8 = 16. c) 20 − 12 = 8, 8 × 3 = 24. d) 21 + 15 = 36, 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Q2a: 4 × 3 + 2 = 14, 10 × 3 + 2 = 32; 17 − 2 = 15, 15 ÷ 3 = 5; 29 − 2 = 27, 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Q2b: 3 × 2 + 1 = 7, 5 × 2 + 1 = 11, 10 × 2 + 1 = 21, 20 × 2 + 1 = 41. (Finding a hidden rule from a table is Think harder 1.)

p2l5-teachparts.note: Minutes 55 to 57.5. Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q4 uses 3 equal bags instead of 2 halves; do not do Q4 for them). Fold a paper strip in half to show the two equal parts, then fold one half again unevenly for "used" and "left". Common mistake: answering 14 (one half) instead of 28. Ask: "Is 14 ALL her beads, or one part?"

p2l5-teachorder.note: Minutes 57.5 to 59.5. Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q5). The top machine is A, the bottom one is B. Children predict first, then click for each OUT. Then step 1 and step 2. Check step 2 forwards: 6 × 3 = 18, 18 + 6 = 24. Link to the explore: "Remember swapping your two cards?"

p2l5-ws2.note: Minutes 59.5 to 71. Children work alone. Note who needs a short catch-up next lesson. Check that every child draws bars for Q3 and Q4. Q6 (three children, 40 marbles) is now Think Harder 4 for any child who would like more; the slide before the Stretch slide teaches the method. Tutor rule at minute 59.5: if the clock is more than 2 minutes late, drop the last Core question of page 2 to take-home (children draw a star beside it). Never shorten talk time, the exit ticket, looking back or the closing. Questions marked with a star and the words take-home on the page are done at home; their answers are still on the check-together slide.

p2l5-ws2ans.note: Minutes 71 to 73.5. Click after a child explains. Q3 check: 59 − 24 = 35, 35 + 15 = 50. Q4: one bag had 10 before 4 were taken out; 10 + 10 + 10 = 30. Q5: Mei (5 + 4) × 2 = 18; Ali 5 × 2 + 4 = 14; for Ali to get 18: 18 − 4 = 14, 14 ÷ 2 = 7.

p2l5-teachthree.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Teach for Think Harder 4 (three children and 40 marbles), after page 2 is checked. Draw Tom’s bar first: the other two are "Tom’s bar and a bit more". Cover the yellow extras with your hand: "If nobody had the extras, there would be 25 − 3 − 4 = 18, in three equal bars." Then give the extras back. Common mistake: 25 ÷ 3 straight away (it does not even work).

p2l5-stretch.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Open to any child who chooses it (the choice after question 3 on the worksheet). These are the SAME four questions as the printed Think harder page: the slide shows 1 to 3 and question 4 is on the page only. Never announce who is working on which page. Answers: 1) × 3, then + 5. IN 10 gives OUT 35. OUT 26 comes from IN 7 (26 − 5 = 21, 21 ÷ 3 = 7). 2) $36. Undo the last step: dad gave him as much as he had left, so $42 is two equal bars of $21. So Ben had $21 after the book, and $21 + $15 = $36 at first. Check: 36 − 15 = 21, 21 + 21 = 42. 3) 36 (30 − 12 = 18 is half, 18 + 18 = 36) 4) (Question: Ali, Ben and Siti have 40 marbles altogether. Ben has 5 more marbles than Ali. Siti has 8 more marbles than Ali. How many marbles does each child have? Draw a bar for each child.) Ali 9, Ben 14, Siti 17 (40 − 5 − 8 = 27, 27 ÷ 3 = 9; check 9 + 14 + 17 = 40)

p2l5-challenge.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Pairs try first, then use the "see it" slide if stuck, then the walk-through. Ask for the reason every time. Answers: 1) 6 (go back twice: 12 + 4 = 16, 16 ÷ 2 = 8; 8 + 4 = 12, 12 ÷ 2 = 6; check 6 → 8 → 12). 2) Ben 25, Ali 15 (give the 5 back: Ben 20 + 5, Ali 20 − 5). Ben had 10 more than Ali, not 5, because Ben lost 5 AND Ali gained 5. Extension: if Ben had given 8 and they ended equal, he had 16 more at first (the gap is double the number given). Common wrong answer for 2: "both had 20" or "Ben 25, Ali 20", or "5 more".

p2l5-chdiag.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Show after pairs have tried, or if they are stuck. The pictures show the problem, not the answer. Ask: What do you notice? What do we know? Where do we start? (At the end: the 12, and the two bars of 20.) Which bar was longer before? How do you know?

p2l5-chwalk.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Use after pairs have tried. Q1: the machine runs twice, so we undo it twice, starting from the final OUT; the number in the middle is 8. Q2: the last thing that happened was "Ben gives 5", so we undo it: Ben takes 5 back and Ali gives 5 back. Ask: "Why is the difference 10 and not 5?" (Ben lost 5 AND Ali gained 5.)

p2l5-talk.note: Minutes 76.5 to 81.5. Pairs talk for 90 seconds, then two volunteers share. Make them test both ways. Answer: Mei is right: 20 − 6 = 14, 14 ÷ 2 = 7, and 7 × 2 + 6 = 20. Ali gets 20 ÷ 2 = 10, 10 − 6 = 4, but 4 × 2 + 6 = 14, not 20. The last step happened last, so it is undone first. Praise the reasons, not only the answers. Talk time rules: you choose volunteers first ("Who would like to share?"); never cold-call a child by name; any child may say pass; no public tallies, scores or rankings.

p2l5-exit.note: Minutes 81.5 to 86.5. Answer: 5 (14 + 6 = 20, 20 ÷ 4 = 5; check 5 × 4 = 20, 20 − 6 = 14). Extension: make a three-step machine with a × card, a ÷ card and a + card for a partner. Children keep slips on their desks and tick them against the answer on the next click; nothing is held up. About 2 minutes of child work.

p2l5-reflect.note: SPINE: Minutes 86.5 to 88.5. Start the timer (120 seconds). Say: "Pick one problem from today. Question 1: did I answer the question? Question 2: does my answer make sense? Question 3: can I check it another way? Tick, write one line, or pass. If you are still stuck, tick the box and I will come." Children tick the Look back box on the Choose and look-back page of their workbook, or just tick on paper. A pass is always allowed. It is never marked, never collected in front of the group and never read out; the tutor may look at it afterwards. If a child ticks "I am still stuck", check in during the open session next lesson (a quick visit to the shared breakout room or a hand signal, with a parent nearby; never a direct message). Do not ask children to share. Praise a check you saw, not speed. Then stamp the journals. After the look-back, minutes 88.5 to 90 are flex time (the buffer): finish stamps, then goodbye. Do not start anything new.
